report:
Reviewed the complete interface_dependencies claim, both associated implementation files, and both test entries. Captured the checking design, the accepted cross-item interface RFD decision, trace-producing metadata fixture, body-forcing/root-setup helpers, and Salsa execution-log collection/draining. This was source inspection; no behavioral suite was rerun and no source was changed.

The claim permits a body's own CST/signature and demanded resolution, interface, metadata, candidate and solver facts, while forbidding any callee-body dependency. LocalFnSym::body reads self.sig and self.cst, constructs a fresh checking context and scope, imports signature types/environment, binds parameters, checks its own body, coerces against its declared return type and finalizes. It does not iterate over other function bodies. In expr.rs, a local function reference uses local.sig, instantiates that signature and submits its parameter environment before constructing FnPtr. Direct calls consume parameter and return types from that interface; method syntax delegates provider resolution instead of invoking a callee body. These inspected entry paths respect the boundary. The RFD permits coarse inputs to cause provisional extra execution while semantic backdating stops unchanged interfaces propagating; I do not confuse that qualification with permission to read another body.

The ordinary clone_method_body_has_a_narrow_reusable_semantic_query_trace test is meaningful but scoped. force_db_method finds the requested DbDropGuard::db method, demands its body and asserts no diagnostics. BuiltinDeriveTcx records calls in a shared log. On the cold request the test requires an exact sorted list of selected associated-items, function-signature and trait-signature calls, forbids metadata call labels containing body, requires the separate external item-name read, and verifies a body query actually executed. On the unchanged warm request it asserts no metadata calls and no body-query execution. The captured Database implementation logs WillExecute and drains the log, so the warm assertion measures execution reuse rather than a stale repeated log.

The test does not whitelist every cold Salsa dependency, does not prove every local callee body is absent merely by checking external metadata names, and does not cover persistent edits. Those limits align with the explicitly associated checking_body_interface_dependencies TODO: complete cold semantic-fact whitelists excluding all callee bodies/unrelated interfaces, unchanged warm no-work behavior across representative cases, and persistent edits distinguishing relevant interface changes from unrelated body changes. Its prerequisite is the full claim-specific trace/edit matrix. That TODO contains no assertions and remains visibly deferred; the ordinary clone case is not upgraded into exhaustive proof of all transitive body-checker dependencies. All implementation and evidence entries and all claim categories are accounted for. No concrete defect was identified in the reviewed paths, and no additional edits are requested.
